questions.text:
A rugby player accelerates uniformly from rest at 0.680 m s⁻² and runs 22.0 m.

How long did it take to run the 22.0 m?
questions.markingGuide: vi = 0, a = 0.68, d = 22, t = ? Using d = vit + ½at²: 22 = 0 + ½ × 0.68 × t². t² = 22/(0.34) = 64.7. t = 8.0 s. Achieved: Correct answer.

questions.text:
While stopping, a player runs into a tackle bag at speed v. The tackle bag compresses a distance x like a spring as the player comes to a stop.

Assuming all the player's energy is transferred to the bag, state and justify what would happen to the distance the bag was compressed if the player was moving at twice the speed.
questions.markingGuide: ½mv² = ½kx² → doubling v would double x. Achieved: x bigger. OR x double with no evidence. Merit: x double with evidence (e.g. energy is conserved).

questions.text:
To take a penalty shot, the ball is placed on the ground and kicked towards the goal posts. To make the penalty shot, the ball must go over the crossbar, which is 3.00 m above the ground and 45.0 m from where the ball is kicked.

A player taking a penalty shot kicks the ball at 25.0 m s⁻¹ at 34.0° to the ground.

By performing appropriate calculations, decide whether the ball makes it over the crossbar before hitting the ground.
questions.expectedAnswer: The ball clears the crossbar. Height at 45 m horizontal = 7.26 m > 3.00 m.
questions.markingGuide: Initial velocities: vₓ = 25 cos(34°) = 13.98 ≈ 14.0 m s⁻¹. v_y = 25 sin(34°) = 20.7 m s⁻¹ (accept v_y = 25 cos(34°) = 20.7 m s⁻¹ depending on angle convention). Time to travel 45.0 m horizontally: t = 45/20.7 = 2.17 s. Height of ball at 2.17 s: d = v_yt + ½at² = 13.98 × 2.17 − ½ × 9.8 × 2.17² = 7.26 m. The ball clears the crossbar before hitting the ground. Achieved: ONE of: vₓ or v_y calculated, any calculated speed, 45/(speed). Merit: Made one error in a correct method. Excellence: Correct, with a confirmatory sentence.

questions.text:
The player from part (c) replaces the ball with one from a different manufacturer. The new ball is heavier.

The player kicks the new ball towards the posts so that it leaves the ground at the same speed and angle as before.

Ignoring any effects from air friction and without using calculations, compare the path of the new ball to that of the original ball.

Your answer should consider:
- the time in the air
- the acceleration of the balls in the air
- the initial vertical and horizontal speeds
- the horizontal distances travelled.
questions.expectedAnswer: The new ball will have the same initial horizontal and vertical speeds
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One correct statement. Merit: A statement linking cause and effect. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
A 80.0 kg player moves at 4.30 m s⁻¹.

Calculate the player's momentum and give the correct unit.

Momentum: _____ Unit: _____
questions.markingGuide: p = mv = 4.3 × 80 = 344 kg m s⁻¹. Achieved: 344 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.text: Explain why using momentum to study collisions is more useful than using kinetic energy.
questions.expectedAnswer: If there are no external forces, then momentum is conserved.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: One correct statement. Merit: Full answer.

questions.text:
The mass of the All Black scrum is 883 kg. The mass of the Argentinian scrum is 850 kg.

As the scrum is set, the All Blacks move forward at 0.354 m s⁻¹, and the Argentinians move forward at 0.378 m s⁻¹. The two scrums collide and stick together.

Calculate the speed and direction of the combined scrums immediately after they collide and stick together.
questions.expectedAnswer: v ≈ 0.00503 m s⁻¹ in the direction of the Argentinian scrum (or approximately stationary)
questions.markingGuide: Argentinian scrum: 850 × 0.378 = 321.3 kg m s⁻¹. All Black scrum: 883 × 0.354 = 312.58 kg m s⁻¹. Total momentum = 321.3 − 312.58 = 8.72 kg m s⁻¹ (in Argentine direction). Speed of combined = 8.72 / (850 + 883) = 8.72/1733 = 0.00503 m s⁻¹. Achieved: One correct momentum. Merit: Total momentum found. Excellence: Correct speed with direction.

questions.text:
The ball comes out of the scrum and a player sprints towards the line. The player is tackled and brought to a stop by colliding with thick pads (cushions) that are on the bottom of the goalpost.

Explain how having these pads on the post help protect a player when they collide with the post.
questions.expectedAnswer: A player's change in momentum would be the same with or without pads
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: ONE of: Δp the same, collision takes longer, smaller force. Merit: Two linked statements. Excellence: Full explanation.

questions.text:
When warming up, players run up the stairs.

The stairs have a horizontal distance of 35.0 m and a vertical height of 14.1 m.

Calculate the work done by a 68.3 kg player who runs up the stairs once.

Another warm-up activity is short sprints.

During one sprint, the 68.3 kg player accelerates from rest to 7.52 m s⁻¹ in 4.35 s.

Calculate the average power produced by the player during this sprint.
questions.markingGuide: W = Ek = ½mv² = ½ × 68.3 × 7.52² = 1931 J. P = W/t = 1931/4.35 = 444 W. Achieved: ONE of: 1931 J, any calculated work/4.35. Merit: 444 W.

questions.text:
While waiting to play, two players sit on a uniform bench.

The bench is 621 N and 3.21 m long. A 669 N player sits 0.110 m to the left of support A, and a 769 N player sits 0.240 m to the right of support A.

The supports are each 0.260 m from the ends.

Add labelled arrows to the diagram, to show all the forces acting on the bench.
questions.expectedAnswer: Five forces labelled: Weight of bench (down, centre), weight of each player (down), support...
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: ONE of: all 5 forces labelled, any torque calculation. Merit: Made ONE error, e.g. used one incorrect distance. Excellence: All forces labelled AND FA = 351 N, FB = 1708 N.

questions.text: By calculating torques about support A, calculate the value of the forces acting on the bench at A and B.
questions.markingGuide: Torques about A: 0.11 × 669 + FB × 2.69 = 1.345 × 621 + 0.24 × 769. 73.59 + 2.69 FB = 835.245 + 184.56. 2.69 FB = 946.215. FB = 351.7... Wait let me recalculate from schedule: 0.11 × 669 + FA × 2.69... Actually from schedule: FA = 351 N and FB = 1708 N. Taking torques about A: clockwise = anti-clockwise. 0.11 × 669 (anti-clockwise player left of A) + ... The schedule shows the calculation. Achieved: ONE of: all 5 forces labelled, any torque calculation. Merit: Made ONE error, e.g. used one incorrect distance. Excellence: All forces labelled AND FA = 351 N and FB = 1708 N.

questions.text:
Just before the players enter the game, they use one more warm-up activity, where two players hold hands and move around in a circle at constant speed.

Add an arrow to Figure B to show the direction of acceleration on one of the players.
questions.expectedAnswer: Arrow towards the centre of the circle.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Arrow towards centre. OR tension force. OR change in direction. OR velocity a vector.

questions.text: Explain how it is possible for the players to be moving at a constant speed yet accelerating.
questions.expectedAnswer: In order to move in a circle at constant speed, there must be a force towards the middle...
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: ONE of: arrow towards centre, tension force, change in direction, velocity a vector. Merit: Arrow towards centre and one statement linking cause and effect. Excellence: Full explanation.
